clinician.trajectory_summary: A 52-year-old woman presented with respiratory symptoms and fever, leading to a diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with new-onset pancytopenia and febrile neutropenia. Initial laboratory hemogram confirmed pancytopenia (E001). A rectal swab on admission was positive for carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae colonization (E002). On day +8 after chemotherapy (CH), she developed distal thrombophlebitis with cutaneous bacterial infection, which was treated (E003). On day +11 after CH, she developed fever, elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 30 mg/mL, procalcitonin 16 ng/mL), and vulvar pain, swelling, pruritus, with a hard and painful phlegm in the right outer labia and exuberant inflammatory signs (E004). Blood cultures and vulvar exudate analysis on day +11 isolated carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, resistant to meropenem and amikacin, and sensitive to tigecycline and colistin (E005). A pelvic CT scan on day +12 showed no liquid or air collections (E006). Subsequently, the surgical team performed superficial debridement of the soft tissue above the fascia of the pubic area extending towards the right paragenital area, followed by ICU admission due to multiorgan dysfunction (E007). On day seven after surgery, recurrence of local infiltration with cellulitis of the surgical borders and increased inflammatory markers motivated new antibiotic rotation (E009).
